### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `packages/rest/src/stale-summary-answer.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via CloneDataResponseSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via CloneDataResponseSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `packages/rest/src/stale-summary-answer.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `applyDroppedFieldsHeader (5 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a51c90efc8d05c204fe889617ca3dd8e5bf2e46` — the merge of head `a6b0d839d45a4e08037beab8bd4efb60b2fcb369` into base `ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a51c90efc8d05c204fe889617ca3dd8e5bf2e46 && git checkout 8a51c90efc8d05c204fe889617ca3dd8e5bf2e46
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f a6b0d839d45a4e08037beab8bd4efb60b2fcb369 && git checkout -B drift-repro ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f && git merge --no-ff a6b0d839d45a4e08037beab8bd4efb60b2fcb369

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a6b0d839d45a4e08037beab8bd4efb60b2fcb369`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/batch.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/stale-summary-answer.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts (read, untouched), packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts (read, untouched), packages/client/src/index.ts, content/docs/api/data-api.mdx, content/docs/references/api/batch.mdx, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, .changeset/28933-dropped-fields-header-every-write-door.md, packages/rest/src/rest-dropped-fields-every-write-door.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-static-readonly.dogfood.test.ts

Face: `schema` (the recogniser's `hits` are the two `packages/spec/src/**` files; both are `.describe()` text only — no key, type, optionality or status changes). PR #29034, branch `claude/project-thread-gibefk`, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, one commit over merge-base `135054eb`. Reviewed read-only: the net diff against `main` at the head, card #28933 with every comment, #3431, #3455 (its landing PR #3468's changeset), #15703 (its landing PR #16823), and the head's check-runs. The dispatch order was not an input to the judgments below.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The published spec surface (the `hits`).** `BatchOperationResultSchema.droppedFields` (batch.zod.ts), `CloneDataResponseSchema.droppedFields` and `CreateManyDataResponseSchema.droppedFields` (protocol.zod.ts) change `.describe()` prose only: "REST does not emit `X-ObjectStack-Dropped-Fields` for batches" / "sets no `X-ObjectStack-Dropped-Fields` header" become "REST also sends the header, naming the union (each field and reason once)" / "REST additionally surfaces this as the header". No accept set moves: every request schema is untouched and every response member keeps its key, type and optionality. **Right** — and required, because the old text became false the moment the routes changed; a `.describe()` that promises the absence of a header the route now sends would be a spec stating a falsehood. `git grep` on the head tree finds no remaining "body only / no header" carrier outside CHANGELOGs.

2. **One seam, byte-identical single answers.** `applyDroppedFieldsHeader(res, result, rows?)` (error-response.ts) now reads `result.droppedFields` plus each `rows[i].droppedFields`, and `droppedFieldsHeaderValue` builds the value through a `Set` of `field;reason=REASON` tokens joined by `', '` in insertion order. The old formatter was `flatMap` + `join(', ')` over the same tokens. For a single-record answer the two are byte-identical unless the producer emitted the same (field, reason) pair twice; `createData` / `updateData` / `cloneData` (protocol.ts) push one engine `onFieldsDropped` event per strip point, so no duplicate exists on a single write, and the pre-existing #3431 suite is unedited. The union format is #3431's grammar, unchanged: same token, same separator. Neither function is exported from `@objectstack/rest`'s index, so the signature change is internal. **Right.**

3. **Coverage of every 2xx write answer carrying `droppedFields`.** The REST write doors at the head and their answers: `POST /data/:object` and `PATCH /data/:object/:id` (header, pre-existing); `POST /data/:object/:id/clone` (now the seam, success and stale-roll-up 201); `POST /data/:object/createMany` (seam, success and stale-roll-up 201); `POST /data/:object/batch` and `/updateMany` (seam over `result.results`); `POST /data/:object/import` commit (seam over `summary.results`); cross-object `POST /batch` (seam over the top-level `droppedFields`). Doors whose answers carry no `droppedFields`, read in the cited code: `/deleteMany`, `/import/jobs` (201 `{ jobId, object, status, total, createdAt }`), `/import/jobs/:jobId/cancel` (`{ success }`), `/import/jobs/:jobId/undo` (`{ success, jobId, deleted, restored, failed, failures }`), public `/forms/:slug/submit` (`{ id, fields? }` — its `droppedFields` is dropped by the #22437 projection, so `earnedAnswerLogged` without the header is correct there), and single delete's stale-roll-up answer (no drops on a delete). The `PATCH` / `DELETE` single doors' stale answers already went through `earnedWriteDespiteStaleSummary`. **No 2xx write answer that carries `droppedFields` is left without the header.** The runtime dispatcher's `POST`/`PATCH /data` arms (`packages/runtime`) are a different package and door family, not this card's; the dev's "noted, not filed" is the right disposition, and the seat may file it when reach is measured.

4. **Bodies unchanged byte for byte.** Every call is placed between the protocol result and `res.json(...)` of the same object; the only body-adjacent edit is the cross-object batch's literal becoming `const answer = { results, ...droppedFields? }` with the same keys in the same order. The stale-roll-up branches return the same `earned` object as before. The seam writes only a header and returns before touching `res` when the value is empty, so **no header is sent when nothing was stripped**; the new suite has a no-strip control for clone, createMany, updateMany + batch, import commit and cross-object batch, and the dogfood pin one for createMany. **Right.**

5. **The reversal of #3455.** PR #3468's changeset and the three describe texts said the header is "deliberately not emitted for batches — one response header cannot express per-row drops, so the per-row body field is the canonical bulk channel". That stance was a design rationale, not an acceptance-set guarantee a client could consume: the body remains the canonical per-row channel and is unchanged, the header is additive on the wire, and a client that inferred "nothing stripped" from the header's absence on a bulk door was already wrong by that same text. The new describe text keeps the honest half ("a single response header cannot say which row dropped what") and states the union. **Right**, and the changeset says so in words.

6. **File surface wider than the claim.** The claim named `crud-routes.ts`; the card's "around L304 and L495" are the single create / update calls, which were correct at main, but the clone and createMany handlers live in `data-action-routes.ts` and `batch-routes.ts` after #23050's split. The nine non-test, non-prose files touched are: the seam (error-response.ts), the six doors (batch-routes.ts, data-action-routes.ts), a comment on the twin helper (stale-summary-answer.ts), a comment on the re-export (rest-server.ts), the three describe texts and the client docblock (words that went false), data-api.mdx (same), and the two regenerated reference pages (`gen:docs` output; `check:generated` would red without them). Each is either the ruling's "measure the other write doors and give them the same call" or a carrier that would otherwise state the opposite of what the tree does. **Justified; nothing unrelated rides along.**

7. **Evidence, as claimed and as checkable read-only.** The ablation table (11 legs) is consistent with the committed 15-case file: "each token once" reds exactly the four doors whose events repeat a field (updateMany, batch, import, cross-object; createMany's body is already a union), "per-row reading" reds the three `results[i]` doors, each door leg reds its own cases. The 106-line `dispatch-gates --ran` list in the seat's copy carries 106 `exit 0`. One count does not reconcile: the committed file has five no-strip control cases by my reading (clone, createMany, updateMany + batch, import commit, cross-object), so red-first on main reads as 10 red / 5 green rather than the reported 11 / 4; the difference is one control case, most likely a later edit to the file after the red-first run, and the head's gates, not the red-first count, are the verdict. Overlap: all 45 open PRs' file lists were read through the REST API; none touches any of this PR's non-test files or the dogfood file (the dev's #28731 reading holds).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28933-dropped-fields-header-every-write-door.md`: `@objectstack/rest` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/client` patch, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body. **Matches the diff.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is **right**: the public surface gains a response header on six answers; nothing previously accepted is refused, nothing previously produced is removed, no status changes. Not `(narrowing)`: the #3455 reversal removes a documented absence, not a guarantee (judgment 5).
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is **right**: describe text on response schemas changes nothing a metadata author can write; no key added, tombstoned, re-valued or re-defaulted.
- `patch` follows AGENTS.md step 3: kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. #15703's "minor under the bump-level rule" predates the current level table and concerned adding a member; this diff adds none. No ADR-0087 marker is owed (not breaking). The changeset states the union-versus-per-row limit as the ruling asked.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question — import dry run sends no header (shipped as option A).** Recommendation: **keep A.** The header's #3431 meaning is "fields stripped from THIS write"; a `dryRun: true` answer is a 200 preview that wrote nothing, so a header there would say a write dropped fields when no write happened, and the rows already preview the strip in `results[i].droppedFields`. The guard is one line and the import case pins both arms, so if the seat rules B it is a one-line flip with the pin's expectation inverted; the changeset already states the dry-run behaviour, so no further carrier needs editing for A.
- **Dev finding (3) — a plain clone reports the source's null readonly columns as dropped, and the header now repeats it.** This is a producer defect on main (`cloneData` copies null readonly columns; the engine's strip reports a present key whatever its value), measured by the dev on main at `135054eb` and on the stock showcase. The header is, by the ruling, a mirror of what the body reports; having the seam filter what the body says would create a second policy on the one seam. **Separate card**, class a, fix site on the producer side (clone's copy or the strip's "present key" reading), with the dev's dedupe words; this PR neither causes nor widens the defect beyond mirroring the body it already carried, and the test file's clone cases and the dogfood `toContain` assertion are the right accommodation. The seat should file it before or at landing so the mirror has a tracked producer fix.
- **Dev finding (4) — the card's createMany path.** The card and triage's note wrote the bare-array createMany as `POST /data/:object`; that route refuses an array body (400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, #3899). The real bare-array door is `POST /data/:object/createMany`, which is what the PR fixes and the dogfood pin hits. **Premise correction, not a premise failure**: the defect (body `droppedFields`, no header) was real on the actual door, so `premise_still_valid: true` stands in substance; the record notes the path so the card's repro step 3 is read as `/createMany`.
- **The runtime dispatcher twin** (`packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts`, no header even for single create/update): outside this card's REST doors; reach unmeasured. Not a flag against this PR; the seat may file it once reach is measured.
- **CI state on the head at review time:** 38 check-runs completed (26 success, 12 skipped), 0 failed, 29 still in progress (Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Build Core, Type Check workspace and consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI). Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Lint ESLint, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Spec property liveness and Dogfood Regression Gate are green. The landing check "all checks green" is the seat's at enqueue; this review's verdict does not depend on it and nothing red exists to be read as by-design.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no human login to name.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-gibefk`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**
